question: GQ-001
scope: the enforcement and memory layers of one agent workspace, measured over a single continuous session

enforcement.finding: Gates and execution caught comparable numbers of defects. The gates catch drift between a recorded value and its source; they cannot catch code that does not do what its description claims, a wrong path shared by producer and checker, or a diagnosis that names the wrong layer. Those were all found by running something.
enforcement.count_reconciliation: An initial looser grep returned 5; counting each phrase separately gave 'gate caught'=2, 'evaluator flagged'=1, others 0, union=3. The higher figure matched prose discussing gates rather than gate events. 3 is the reproducible number and is used here.

memory.finding: Durable state is the workspace's memory; the session's context is not. A prior handover written to this agent contained two load-bearing claims that were false within twelve hours, so memory must be dated and supersedable rather than authoritative.

caveats: n=1 session, one agent, one repository.
Defect counts come from grepping my own worklogs for admission phrases; a defect I failed to notice or record is invisible to this measurement.
'Caught by execution' and 'caught by a gate' were classified by keyword, not by re-reading each worklog.
source: this repository, anchored at commit d1c90dbd (HEAD at measured_at)
derivation_note: These are point-in-time counts of a growing session: 54 commits then, 88 now. A live derivation would report a permanent false mismatch, so each query is anchored to the commit that was HEAD at measured_at. Anchored, commits (54) and worklogs (46) re-derive exactly. metrics_files re-derives to 26, not the asserted 27 — one metrics file was on disk but untracked when the snapshot was taken, so the filesystem count included it and git does not. The asserted number was true of the disk and is not reproducible from history; recorded rather than quietly corrected.
